_comment: Krea-2 LoRA + TAG EMBEDDING over the 5-source tag_samples_clean mix. Adds a learnable per-tag table whose matched tags become extra DiT tokens between the text prefix and the image tokens, so a prompt can carry booru bag-of-words tags and natural language at once. Run: uv run python krea2/train.py krea2/configs/train_pipeline_lora_tags.json
_comment_uncond: COUPLED: the same per-sample coin blanks the caption and masks the tag block, because a CFG negative pass drops both channels at inference.
_comment_lora_exclude: 'tagembed' is appended automatically: the tag projection is new weight trained directly, not a pretrained matrix to adapt.
_comment_tag_embed: 315,966 tags x 512 = 161.8M params (0.31 GB bf16) in the embed chunk, with 1.21 GB of RowAdamW moments parked in host RAM. vocab_path is VERSIONED: its row count is written into the checkpoint and asserted on load, because rebuilding the corpus renumbers the id space and would silently train against shifted meanings — bump to tags_v2.parquet rather than overwriting. max_tags is free anywhere in 1..256 (the DiT pads the combined sequence to a multiple of 256), and typical booru rows carry ~44 tags. tag_drop_prob drops the tag block ALONE, which is what teaches the model that a caption with no tags is still a valid prompt.
_comment_data: The same 5-source mix the teacher was fine-tuned on. 'tags' is exactly 100% present on the boorus and exactly 0% elsewhere, so the non-booru sources supply the untagged case with no synthetic handling — an untagged row is a bit-exact no-op.

parquet_dataloader._comment_captions: Weights are CONDITIONAL, not global: a row is drawn from whichever of these columns it actually has, re-normalized. So 0.25 on brief_summary does not buy 25% natural-language captions overall, it buys 25% of the rows that have one. The case that makes the table earn its keep is a booru row drawing a natural-language caption while its full tag set rides along.
parquet_dataloader._comment_tag_column: DECOUPLED from caption_columns: tags are read from here whichever caption column was sampled.
